title: Model pin arbitration and client pin-expression surface
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Customers need an unambiguous, ergonomic way to pin which model artifact the runtime should resolve at request time. Current SDK surface supports simple strings (e.g. "gptx-latest") but lacks a formal grammar and runtime arbitration rules for conflicting or ambiguous expressions (tag vs semver range vs commit hash). This causes client confusion, unexpected rollouts, and difficulty publishing performance profiles tied to specific pins.

Goal: Define a single pin-expression grammar, runtime arbitration semantics, SDK validation behavior, and performance-profile binding rules. Deliverables: API/SDK surface spec, runtime resolution priority matrix, validation & helpful error codes, migration guidance for customers, and telemetry/reporting to detect ambiguous or stale pins.
acceptance_criteria: Pin-expression grammar documented with examples for tag, semver, semver range, and commit-ref
Runtime resolves pins deterministically with a documented priority matrix (exact hash > semver range > semver exact > tag > default), including fallback rules
SDK surfaces client-side validation with clear, actionable error messages and warnings for deprecated or ambiguous syntax
Publishing a performance profile may pin it to either a commit-hash or semver range; UI shows pin binding and warns on profile-model mismatch
Telemetry emits events when runtime falls back from requested pin to a different artifact (reason + resolution path)
Migration doc and compatibility tests (unit + e2e) exist and pass
design_decisions: Use a single string-based pin-expression grammar instead of separate typed fields to minimize API churn
Treat commit-hash (full or prefix) as highest-fidelity pin that cannot be fuzzy-resolved; if absent, semver-range resolution occurs next
Semver ranges follow npm-style precedence semantics (e.g., ^, ~, >=, <=); runtime will select the highest matching version unless 'lowest' policy is requested
Tags are lightweight labels that map to the latest matching release of a channel; tags are lowest precedence and always allow fallback to other variants
Performance profiles published by onboarders should optionally include an explicit artifact-ref; if omitted, profile is linked to the model family + tag used during evaluation
SDKs should expose both a strict parsing mode (throws on ambiguous pins) and a tolerant mode (logs warning and allows runtime fallback)
pin_expression_examples: commit:3f7b9a8e — exact commit hash pin (full or 8-char prefix allowed)
semver:^1.4.0 — semver range pin; runtime picks highest compatible release
tag:stable — channel tag pin (maps to the tag->release mapping managed by model-onboarding)
raw string (legacy): "my-model:latest" — legacy compatibility; SDK validates and rewrites to canonical grammar if possible
runtime_resolution_matrix: 1) If pin expression contains 'commit:' and commit exists -> resolve to that exact artifact
2) Else if expression contains 'semver:' or semver range -> resolve to highest published release satisfying range
3) Else if expression contains 'tag:' -> resolve to the release currently bound to the tag (tag binding is mutable)
4) Else if legacy raw string -> attempt auto-parse into canonical grammar; if ambiguous, behavior depends on SDK mode (strict vs tolerant)
5) If resolution fails and 'allow_fallback' true -> apply fallback policy (try other channels defined in pin_options, then global fallback model pool), emit fallback telemetry
6) If resolution fails and strict -> return 409 with error_code PIN_RESOLUTION_FAILED and human-friendly diagnostics
sdk_changes: Add PinExpression parser utility (languages: Go, Python, TypeScript) with API: parsePin(expression, mode="tolerant")
Expose PinOptions in request payload: { allow_fallback: boolean, prefer_lowest_semver: boolean, telemetry_hint: string } (SDKs map to typed fields; wire still accepts string grammar)
Validation modes: STRICT (throw errors for ambiguous grammar), WARN (log and continue), AUTO_REWRITE (attempt canonical rewrite)
Client library will include migration helper that scans existing requests and flags deprecated patterns (e.g., implicit 'latest' without family)
errors_and_telemetry: Telemetry event 'pin.resolution' emitted with fields: requested_expression, resolved_artifact_ref, resolution_path, fallback_reason (if any), request_id
Dashboard: new chart 'pin fallback rate' per-model-family and per-tag to catch mis-bound tags or stale tags
Alerting: page if >0.5% of requests for a customer are resolved via fallback for >10 minutes

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Semver-range resolution could increase catalog lookups and add latency. Mitigation: add LRU resolution cache keyed by (family, range, catalog-etag) and pre-warm cache during deployment rollouts
Risk: Customers relying on mutable tags may be surprised when a tag is rebound. Mitigation: Console warns on tag rebinds; recommend pinning profiles to commit-hash for reproducible evals

Risk: Migration breakage for legacy clients sending ambiguous raw strings. Mitigation: SDKs ship tolerant parsing by default and a migration scanner that flags customers with high usage of legacy patterns
